svg.title: The ray bench: P1, P2, P9 and RT, two runs
svg.desc: Top: the 4 KB height grid and a ray walking its cells toward the sun, with the cost model C_ray = C_setup + n C_step: predicted 12 to 16 a step and 30 a setup, measured 22.1 and 71 to 76 over two runs. Three panels: P1 cycles a ray against n, measured points with the fit line above the old predicted band; P2 the slice batched, interleaved with the vertex transform, and with the grid in OC-RAM, with both runs; P9 the movers proxy pass, 312 microseconds against a 2 ms slice. Below: RT, four bars of cycles a ray-triangle test, any direction and prepared, with and without early outs, against the assumed 50. Foot: what the two runs change. One console, 2026-11-25.
svg.text: The ray bench: three predictions, run twice on a console
RUN: MEASURED, one console, 2026-11-25, two runs. Images psm-bench-ray1 and ray2. Kernel bytes the same as the reference in every run.
Read from photos PXL_20261125_*: demo/psm/bench/RAY1_RESULTS_*.md and RAY2_RESULTS_*.md; ledger SH4-050 .. 066. THESIS §6 P1, P2, P9; h3; RT.

A town-sized set (1,162 x 64 B = 74 KB) does not fit the 16 KB
TOWN-063 assumed 50 [ESTIMATE]: between the two forms
Prepared saves 47 %; early outs save 46 % (any direction) and 63 % (prepared) [DERIVED].
P1: every §5 cycle count built on 12 .. 16 a step and 30 a setup is low; the slice k and the refresh period P = N / (k f) need redoing.
P2: run the slice batched, before the transform; interleaving costs 16 .. 30 % more a ray. Keep the grid in RAM: OC-RAM's halved cache costs more.
P9: the movers' proxies fit beside one slice. h3, two runs: the DCE batch is 5.7 .. 6.0 % slower than mat_transform in the cache
and 5.5 .. 7.3 % out of it (SH4-065): no measured gain [MEASURED]; whether it stays is the owner's call.
Clocks: the ns clock steps 2.5 ms at each TMU2 reload, once a second (SH4-057, see ns-clock-step): use the cycle counter.
One console. Stand-ins: random receivers, not the town's vertices; a synthetic 28,699-vertex stream. Also OPEN: the clock-read gaps (Q67).
